source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Verapamil lowers serum digoxin concentrations during the first week, so the digoxin dose usually needs to be increased to preserve therapeutic effect.","B":"Verapamil can raise serum digoxin concentrations substantially during the first week, so digoxin levels and toxicity should be monitored and dose reduction considered.","C":"Verapamil changes digoxin absorption but not serum concentration, so routine monitoring for digoxin toxicity is unnecessary when the drugs are combined.","D":"Verapamil prevents digitalis toxicity by increasing digoxin clearance, so the combination permits higher digoxin doses without extra monitoring for toxicity or drug levels."}}
source_row.rationale: Verapamil labeling reports that chronic verapamil treatment can increase serum digoxin concentrations by about 50–75% during the first week and recommends monitoring and dose reduction as needed to avoid digitalis toxicity. Option B reflects that interaction. Option A reverses the effect. Option C incorrectly says serum concentration is unaffected. Option D incorrectly claims increased clearance and lower toxicity risk.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed VERELAN PM (verapamil hydrochloride) — Drug Interactions, §7.4 Digitalis: chronic verapamil can increase serum digoxin concentrations about 50–75% during the first week; monitor and reduce digoxin dose as needed to avoid toxicity.
